content.text: The verifier confirms the compliant status and cited text are correct, and that the two failed deterministic checks (duration, general-solicitation carve-out) are artifacts of clause absence rather than defects. I'll resubmit with the rationale making that absence-based reasoning explicit, and include p0061 so the record covers every "employee"-adjacent paragraph I ruled out.

input.quote: 10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative.
input.rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant exists anywhere in this Agreement, so the preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already met and no redline is required.

Basis for absence: searches for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") plus a full sweep of every "shall not" obligation returned only three categories of text, none of which restricts hiring: (i) p0061, quoted above, where "employee" appears solely as a relationship descriptor in the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause; (ii) the confidentiality duties at p0048-p0054, which restrict use and disclosure of information, not recruitment of staff; and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects for Deerskin Products (p0037 binding the Company, p0042 binding HDI) rather than the solicitation or hiring of either party's employees.

On the two failed deterministic checks (12-month duration and general-solicitation carve-out): these are not defects. Both test attributes that can only exist inside a non-solicit clause. Because there is no such clause, there is no duration to shorten and no carve-out to add. Inserting a carve-out sentence would require first drafting the restrictive covenant it qualifies, which would import a restriction on us that the counterparty never asked for and move us away from the preferred position. The correct outcome under this rule is therefore no edit, and the rendered paragraphs remain byte-identical to the originals.

Separate note for the deal team, outside NOSOLICIT scope: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 does bind us during the term, and it is asymmetric in our favour only as to duration - HDI's mirror covenant at p0042 runs for the term plus two years and survives under Section 10.7, while ours is term-only. That competition restriction should be reviewed under the applicable exclusivity/non-compete rule.
